**A 300-400 W panel array refills a 1,000 Wh power station from empty in about one sunny day. A 200 W panel does it in roughly a day and a half to two days.**

**The formula** (several sources agree on it):
Panel watts ≈ capacity ÷ (peak sun hours × ~0.7-0.75)

Panels rarely deliver their rated watts because of heat, angle, and charge-controller losses ([Enough Watts](https://enoughwatts.com/guides/how-much-solar-to-recharge), [Power Runtime](https://power-runtime.pages.dev/guides/solar-charging/)).

**Panel watts for a full recharge in one day (1,000 Wh)** ([Power Runtime](https://power-runtime.pages.dev/guides/solar-charging/)):
- 3 peak sun hours: ~450 W
- 4 peak sun hours: ~340 W
- 5 peak sun hours: ~270 W
- 6 peak sun hours: ~230 W

**Other scenarios:**
- Held in Reserve estimates about 300 W in good summer sun and 700 W or more in a northern winter ([source](https://www.heldinreserve.com/power/solar-panels-recharge-power-station/)).
- A 200 W panel gives about 600-630 Wh on an average day, so a full recharge takes about 1.5-2 days ([Watt48](https://www.watt48.com/guides/solar-panel-charging-power-station), [Power Preflight](https://powerpreflight.com/guides/solar-panel-sizing-portable-power-stations/)).

**Before you buy:**
- **Solar input limit:** Check your station's maximum solar input. Mid-range 1,000 Wh units often accept 400-800 W, but some cap at 200 W, and extra panel wattage beyond the cap adds nothing.
- **Voltage window:** Make sure the panel's voltage fits your station's input range (often around 12-60 V). Exceeding it can damage the station.
- **Peak sun hours:** Plan around your worst month, not the average. Most of the US gets about 3-6 peak sun hours a day.

If you tell me which power station you have, I can help find a compatible panel.
